name: iqtree3
why: Maximum-likelihood phylogenetics lets you reconstruct evolutionary trees from real sequence data at home.

brief.what_it_is: IQ-TREE 3 is command-line phylogenetics software that reconstructs evolutionary trees by maximum likelihood from sequence alignments. It accepts common alignment formats including PHYLIP, FASTA, Nexus, Clustal and MSF. It writes a human-readable report file with the suffix .iqtree and a Newick tree file named .treefile, which can be opened in viewers such as FigTree, Dendroscope or iTOL. The README also describes built-in ultrafast bootstrap support, automatic model selection, and an alignment simulator called AliSim.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says IQ-TREE succeeded IQPNNI and TREE-PUZZLE and was motivated by the rapid accumulation of phylogenomic data, which called for software that handles large datasets and more complex models of sequence evolution.
brief.how_it_works: The README describes a fast, stochastic tree-search algorithm for maximum-likelihood estimation that can use multicore machines and distributed parallel computing. It checkpoints automatically so an interrupted analysis can resume. Branch support is estimated with the UFBoot ultrafast bootstrap approximation, and models are chosen with ModelFinder. The README does not give more detail on the internals.
brief.install_notes: The README gives no install steps beyond badges. It lists a BioConda package (conda install channel bioconda, package iqtree) as another distribution route. Release binaries are on the GitHub releases page. The web server is an alternative for people who don't want to install anything: the README lists Vienna Bioinformatics Cluster, CIPRES Gateway and Los Alamos hosts. The Homebrew formula's executable is iqtree3.
brief.standout: The breadth of the model library stands out: the README lists common DNA, protein, codon, binary and morphological models, partition models, customisable and empirical mixture models, polymorphism-aware models, and SNP ascertainment-bias correction, all in one tool. It also bundles tests like SH-aLRT, aBayes and AU, plus a simulator that the README says goes beyond Seq-Gen and INDELible.
brief.status: maintained. The repository has active CI and download badges, the README cites a 2026 Molecular Biology and Evolution paper for IQ-TREE 3, and the README's text points to active GitHub discussions and issues. I did not find a last-release date or last-commit date in the README, so the exact recency is unconfirmed.
brief.caveats: The homepage http://www.iqtree.org returned only a redirect page with no target shown, and https://www.iqtree.org/ failed with a URLError, so I read the GitHub README at github.com/iqtree/iqtree3 instead. The README contains a few leftovers from the IQ-TREE 2 repo: user support points to iqtree2 discussions and issues, and the license badge is GPL v2. The mixture models bullet ends with a stray 'and.' The README gives no command examples, so the usage syntax needs checking in the documentation. Some citations are required by feature, so a user of advanced models must cite several papers.
quotes: Efficient and versatile phylogenomic software by maximum likelihood
IQ-TREE automatically performs checkpointing to resume an interrupted analysis.
It is very easy to use with as few as just 3 clicks!
